lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Meal Planning, Cooking, and Food Management
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: cleanup and food-waste reduction

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic cleanup and food-waste reduction task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Looking back over the past few days of meals in the household, the learner records what got thrown away or left half-finished and why, or walks through the usual after-meal cleanup routine step by step, and then picks the single habit most responsible for waste or an incomplete cleanup and rewrites it into a specific new habit to try next week.
materials: adult-or-local: memory of recent meals or the household's usual cleanup routine

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What is the most likely reason this new habit could fail to stick after a week, and what would help you notice if it was slipping?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Specificity of habit identification: The named habit is specific and clearly traced back to something listed in the warm-up or guided task. | Quality of the revised habit: The replacement habit names a concrete action tied to a specific moment, with a clear explanation of why it should help. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner try the new habit for three real days, keep a short log of whether it happened each day, and write a short follow-up on whether the habit reduced waste or improved cleanup as predicted.

resources.title: cleanup and food-waste reduction worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Looking back over the past few days of meals in the household, the learner records what got thrown away or left half-finished and why, or walks through the usual after-meal cleanup routine step by step, and then picks the single habit most responsible for waste or an incomplete cleanup and rewrites it into a specific new habit to try next week.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact cleanup and food-waste reduction decision or action.
Model move 2: Think back over the last several meals before writing anything down.
Model move 3: Walk through the household's usual after-meal cleanup routine step by step, in the order it actually happens, and note where it tends to break down or get skipped.

Model check: Specificity of habit identification: The named habit is specific and clearly traced back to something listed in the warm-up or guided task. | Quality of the revised habit: The replacement habit names a concrete action tied to a specific moment, with a clear explanation of why it should help.

resources.title: cleanup and food-waste reduction action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for cleanup and food-waste reduction.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: cleanup and food-waste reduction coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Looking back over the past few days of meals in the household, the learner records what got thrown away or left half-finished and why, or walks through the usual after-meal cleanup routine step by step, and then picks the single habit most responsible for waste or an incomplete cleanup and rewrites it into a specific new habit to try next week.
Coach direction: Think back over the last several meals before writing anything down.
Learner prompt: List two or three specific things that were thrown away, left uneaten, or forgotten in the refrigerator recently, naming the actual food each time.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: cleanup and food-waste reduction complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Walk through the household's usual after-meal cleanup routine step by step, in the order it actually happens, and note where it tends to break down or get skipped.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I listed the cleanup routine in the actual order it happens, not the order it should happen.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I marked the specific step where cleanup most often gets skipped or rushed.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: cleanup and food-waste reduction minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What is the most likely reason this new habit could fail to stick after a week, and what would help you notice if it was slipping?

Success checks: Specificity of habit identification: The named habit is specific and clearly traced back to something listed in the warm-up or guided task. | Quality of the revised habit: The replacement habit names a concrete action tied to a specific moment, with a clear explanation of why it should help.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: cleanup and food-waste reduction supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional cleanup and food-waste reduction condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Specificity of habit identification: The named habit is specific and clearly traced back to something listed in the warm-up or guided task. | Quality of the revised habit: The replacement habit names a concrete action tied to a specific moment, with a clear explanation of why it should help..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: cleanup and food-waste reduction — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the cleanup and food-waste reduction task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Specificity of habit identification: The named habit is specific and clearly traced back to something listed in the warm-up or guided task. | Quality of the revised habit: The replacement habit names a concrete action tied to a specific moment, with a clear explanation of why it should help.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u03-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
